subject: physics
title: Energy Production Adventure 3: Nuclear reactors and fission
welcome_lead: Today you'll fission uranium and run a reactor.
meta_desc: Physics — nuclear fission, chain reaction, moderator, control rods, fusion potential.
final_note: You learned fission of ²³⁵U releases ~200 MeV per atom; moderator slows neutrons; control rods absorb; fusion (Sun, ITER) merges H to He.

walkthroughs.body_html:
²³⁵U + n → ²³⁶U* → ¹⁴¹Ba + ⁹²Kr + 3n + ~200 MeV.

The ~200 MeV per fission comes from mass defect Δm · c² (binding-energy curve).

1 g of ²³⁵U fissioned ≈ 24,000 kWh — equivalent to 3 tonnes of coal.

- Fuel rods: U-235 enriched (~3-5%).
- Moderator: water/graphite slows neutrons to thermal speeds (more likely to cause fission).
- Control rods: boron/cadmium absorb neutrons to control rate.
- Coolant: removes heat → steam → turbine → generator.

Risks: meltdown (Chernobyl 1986, Fukushima 2011), waste storage.

Sun: 4 ¹H → ⁴He + 2 e⁺ + 2 νₑ + ~26 MeV. Higher binding/nucleon than H.

Earth: ITER (under construction, France) aims for D + T → ⁴He + n + 17.6 MeV.

Needs T ~10⁸ K (plasma magnetically confined).

Benefits: abundant fuel (D from seawater), no long-lived waste — but huge engineering challenge. Global collaboration (35 nations).
